Clump Associations you already have

Source: R/clump.R
og_clump.Rd

og_clump() clumps a data frame of Associations as one set, such as the top hits of several Analyses together, and returns the rows of the index variants (see vignette("ld")).

Usage

og_clump(src, data, ld = NULL, r2 = NULL, kb = NULL)

Arguments

src

A Source, from og_api(). NULL works with a PLINK Reference as ld when nothing is looked up: data has an rsid column, so no ALID needs its rsID from the API. A lookup that is needed without a Source stops, with class opengwasr_source_required.

data

A data frame of Associations, with alid and z, and id for the LD Store to be matched by the Analyses' Assigned Ancestry.

ld

An LD Store's name, an ancestry code (its LD Store), a PLINK Reference from og_plink_reference() (clumped locally by PLINK), or NULL to match the Assigned Ancestry of the Analyses in data (refused, with class opengwasr_ld_unmatched, when they differ, when one is Unassigned, or when data has no id).

r2

The r² above which a variant joins an index variant's clump; NULL for the LD Store's t_far. Required with a PLINK Reference.

kb

The window, in kilobases; NULL for the LD Store's far window. Required with a PLINK Reference.

Value

The rows of data whose variant is an index variant, in their order in data, with columns clump_ld, clump_ld_choice, clump_r2, clump_kb and clump_size (the variants the index variant stands for, itself included), and og_provenance() attached: ld, ld_choice, absent and clump.

Details

Variants are ranked by |z|; a variant listed several times (in several Analyses) is ranked by its largest |z|, and every Association of an index variant is returned. Starting from the strongest, each index variant absorbs every weaker variant within kb kilobases whose r² with it is above r2 (the rule plink --clump uses). Variants the LD Store doesn't hold can't be clumped: they are left out, with a warning of class opengwasr_ld_absent_variants.

r2 and kb default to the LD Store's Far Threshold (t_far) and its far window (far_bp, 10,000 kb), which it can always answer exactly. A pair it can't answer exactly is refused by the API (opengwasr_ld_refusal, with reason, t_far, near_bp and far_bp).

With a PLINK Reference as ld, PLINK clumps on your machine (see og_plink_reference()): r2 and kb are required (there are no defaults to take, so without them it stops, with class opengwasr_plink_settings_required). Variants are matched by rsID, from data's rsid column if it has one, else the GWAS Stores' variant table; those with no rsID match are left out, with a message (class opengwasr_plink_unmatched, count). Provenance's clump names the reference's path as ld, and clump_ld is the same path.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
src <- og_api()
top <- og_tophits(src, c("OGS-00011:GCST90029007", "OGS-00011:GCST90002412"), clump = FALSE)
joint <- og_clump(src, top)
table(joint$id)
} # }
